title: AI scams in Georgia and South Florida: How scammers use deepfakes to steal millions

reading.body:
Scammers are using generative AI and deepfake technology as tools for impersonation fraud. They clone voices from social media posts, spoof phone numbers, and create fake images to pose as immigration attorneys, family members, and other trusted figures. One case involved criminals cloning a South Florida immigration attorney's voice to solicit payment from immigrants for fake legal services. This is a failure at the point of deployment: there is no human verification between the scammer's AI-generated content and the victim's receipt of it.

The attacks succeeded because the victims had no reliable way to verify they were communicating with the person they believed they were. Voice cloning made impersonation more convincing than text-based fraud. The scammers obtained source material, such as social media videos and phone recordings, from public sources and used it without consent. What is not established: whether the platforms hosting the source material, the services that generated the deepfakes, or the communication channels used bear responsibility for the fraud, or what knowledge they had of the misuse.

summary:
Scammers are increasingly using artificial intelligence and deepfake technology to steal money from victims across Georgia and South Florida. According to the FBI's 2025 Internet Crime Report, Americans lost nearly $893 million to AI-enabled scams last year. Notable cases include a South Florida immigration attorney whose voice was cloned to target immigrants, and a Cobb County couple who lost approximately $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam. The FBI received over 1 million internet crime complaints totaling more than $20 billion in losses overall.

Florida reported 350 AI-related complaints with nearly $39.9 million in losses, while Georgia had 71 complaints resulting in more than $10.4 million in losses. Criminals use AI to clone voices from social media, spoof phone numbers, create fake photos, and research personal relationships to make scams more convincing. The grandparent scam, where AI mimics a relative's voice during fake emergencies, has become particularly common. Experts recommend establishing family code words, verifying requests through known phone numbers, and pausing before responding to urgent money requests.
